name: warrant
description: Remove the human from per-item software verification by granting a machine a written, tiered authority and revoking it automatically on evidence. Eight skills: charter (the signed warrant, the only human-signed artifact), oracle (source-to-render lineage, tick-and-tie, taxonomy validation — the deterministic plane, built first because the highest-consequence defect is a correctly rendered screen stating a figure no source supports), assay (mutation survival and cannot-fail patterns, because every downstream verdict inherits the suite's fault sensitivity), panel (one out-of-family grader plus orthogonal lens lanes plus an adjudicator that routes disagreement to arithmetic — deliberately not a jury, since nine judges from seven families supply about two effective votes), feedback (escapes become permanent regression cases; calibration from what got missed rather than from a reader study), lot (risk-limited acceptance of a queue, blind to the machine verdict), ratchet (computes earned tiers, applies revocations without asking, and is a plain script because the component deciding a model's authority should not be the model), and ledger (the hash-chained decision record an auditor reads instead of per-item signatures). Grounded in a 22-source panel across four research backends; every rule traces to a claim id in docs/deep-research/claims.json.
